_: OUR progression rules, as the campaign engine consumes them. Rules and content are separate inputs on purpose: when the whole-game pacing came out wrong (level 4 at hour 19 against Morrowind's 8-12), substituting Morrowind's flat use values into the engine barely moved it, which proved the fault was in the *content* model, not here. Keeping the two apart means the next agent can retune one without silently retuning the other. Anything with a "$from" is READ OUT OF curves.json and is not a second copy of the number - curves.json stays the canonical design-constants file (module 76 §116-129).
label: Elder Souls: Argonia

rankCost._: pointsToNextRank = (skill+1) * classFactor * specFactor. This is Morrowind's own curve, unchanged, which is why the known-answer test can share it.

levelTrigger._: Ten qualifying ranks bank a level; the level lands at the next rest. miscRankDivisor is the 3:1 tail. THE DESIGN BUG FIX: that tail is per-skill and ungated - a misc rank, or a rank in any skill already at 100, is worth 1/3 of a level-credit ALWAYS, not only once every major and minor has reached 100. The old gate discarded roughly two use-points in five.

vastei._: Vastei per rank taken. A skill sitting at 100 keeps earning it from qualifying uses - mastery is not a dead end (this is the second half of the misc/maxed fix).

health._: RETROACTIVE and computed from CURRENT Endurance: maxHealth = attrCoefficient*(Str+End) + level*(levelBase + End/levelEnduranceDivisor). This is the deliberate difference from Morrowind, where the per-level grant is frozen at your level-1 Endurance and raising Endurance late is worthless. NOTE FOR THE ORCHESTRATOR - AN OPEN DIVERGENCE, DELIBERATELY LEFT OPEN. Setting curves.health.levelBase to 0 and levelEnduranceDivisor to 10 is the whole change to reach End/10, and it was tried: it immediately fails `getting-hit-matters` (a legend-tier melee character survives 6 unavoided D5 blows against a target of 3, and best-in-slot armour survives 8 against a 5-7 window). That is the D0-D5 recalibration the orchestrator already owns, not a reason to weaken an invariant, so this file stays on the calibrated value until the ladder is re-solved. Change both together or neither. The detail: module 76 §116-129 states the per-level grant as End/10 flat; curves.json currently carries 1.5 + End/15, which was what the D0-D5 ladder was calibrated against. The two agree to within 2 % up to level 10 and diverge to +18 % at level 50. Switching to End/10 is a one-line change here and in curves.json, but it costs one ladder recalibration - see the report.

worthiness._: OUR anti-grind rule, and the first deliberate difference from Morrowind. It multiplies COMBAT AND DEFENCE use values only: chipping a sponge for 1 % of its health is worth almost nothing, and eating a scratch teaches your armour skill almost nothing. Blocks, casts, brews, locks, persuasions, repairs, enchantments and travel are NOT worthiness-scaled - they are pass/fail verbs with no magnitude to scale by. The per-actor connect damping was removed by owner ruling 2026-08-30: grinding respawning enemies is legitimate play, and no reference game diminishes repeat use.

armourAccrual._: Owner ruling 2026-08-30 (decision 0037): in a game where 3-6 hits kill you, 'learn armour by being hit' is starved and perverse, so armour skills earn from two events, class-weighted. KILLS while wearing the class ('win', keyed to the corpse, never to the encounter ending, so aggro-and-flee teaches nothing; worth scales with the dead thing's health against yours, clamped like offence worthiness) and HITS TAKEN in the class ('hit', the Morrowind rule, kept as a bonus). Light armour learns mostly by winning untouched, heavy mostly by tanking, medium in between; unarmored follows light. Absent in rules-morrowind.json, which keeps pure hit-taken accrual for the known-answer test.

use._: Points delivered per qualifying use. These are Morrowind's own values (UESP Morrowind:Skills and the per-skill pages) - we changed the CONTENT rates, never the exchange rate, so that the known-answer test and our campaign are measuring the same machine. The three Argonia-only entries at the bottom exist because Morrowind has no climbing verb.

weaponConnect._: per connect that deals damage; Axe pays more and Short Blade less, exactly as Morrowind does

use._argoniaOnly: Climbing is a verb Morrowind does not have (world module 76 §122, BotW-style). 1.5 per ten metres puts a 40 m tower at the value of four jumps plus a hard landing, which is about what it costs you in stamina.
